documents.title: H&P - Admission - COPD Exacerbation
lines: ADMISSION H&P
Time of eval: 03:45, HD1
CC: shortness of breath x 3 days, worse tonight
HPI:
74 yo F with GOLD stage III COPD, 40 pack-year hx, quit 6 yrs ago, presents with progressive dyspnea and productive cough.
Sputum turned yellow-green 2 days ago. Increased home albuterol MDI use to q2h with minimal relief.
Denies fever, chest pain, orthopnea, leg swelling. No hemoptysis.
Two prior exacerbations in past 12 months, one requiring admission, none requiring intubation.
Home O2: 2L NC nocturnal only.
ED COURSE:
SpO2 84% at triage; required 4L NC to reach SpO2 89%.
Two albuterol nebulizers in the ED with improved air movement; patient ambulating in hallway before admission decision.
Ipratropium 0.5 mg neb given x2.
ABG at 03:15: pH 7.29, PaCO2 64, PaO2 58 on 4L.
Placed on BiPAP 14/6 at 03:30 for work of breathing.
PMH:
COPD, GOLD III
HTN
Osteoporosis
GERD
Type 2 DM, diet controlled, last A1c 6.4
HOME MEDS:
Tiotropium 18 mcg inh daily
Budesonide/formoterol 160/4.5 two puffs BID
Albuterol MDI 2 puffs q4h prn
Lisinopril 10 mg PO daily
Pantoprazole 40 mg PO daily
Alendronate 70 mg PO weekly
SOCIAL: lives alone in 1-story home, daughter nearby and checks daily. No ETOH. No current tobacco.
ALLERGIES: sulfa - rash
FAMILY HX: father with emphysema
ROS: positive for dyspnea, cough, sputum; negative for fever, chills, chest pain, n/v
EXAM:
T 37.1, HR 108, BP 148/82, RR 32, SpO2 89% on 4L at time of ABG
Gen: elderly female, ill appearing, in distress on BiPAP
Visible accessory muscle use with tripod positioning; respiratory rate 32; speaking 2 to 3 words at a time.
HEENT: mucous membranes dry, no JVD
Lungs: diffuse expiratory wheeze, prolonged expiratory phase, decreased air entry at bases
CV: tachycardic, regular, no murmur
Abd: soft, nontender, BS present
Ext: no edema, no calf tenderness
Neuro: alert, oriented x3, no asterixis
LABS/IMAGING:
WBC 13.2, Hgb 12.8, Plt 288
Na 138, K 4.1, Cl 96, CO2 32, BUN 18, Cr 0.9, glucose 154
CXR: hyperinflation, flattened diaphragms, no focal consolidation or effusion
ECG: sinus tach 108, no acute ischemic changes
ASSESSMENT:
74 yo F with acute exacerbation of COPD with acute on chronic hypercapnic respiratory failure.
PLAN:
1. BiPAP 14/6 per RT, wean as tolerated, repeat ABG in 2h
2. Albuterol/ipratropium neb q4h scheduled, albuterol q2h prn
3. IV steroid: methylprednisolone 40 mg IV every 8 hours
4. Azithromycin 500 mg IV daily
5. Target SpO2 88-92%, avoid overoxygenation
6. Check CBG q6h given steroid burden
7. Telemetry, DVT ppx with enoxaparin 40 mg SQ daily
8. Hold lisinopril if SBP < 100
Discussed with daughter at bedside. Full code.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 AM
lines: PROGRESS NOTE - HD2 07:20
SUBJECTIVE:
Pt reports breathing much improved overnight. Slept intermittently. No chest pain.
Remained on BiPAP continuously for 9 hours, then transitioned to 3L NC at 12:30 on HD1 per RT.
Tolerated NC well through the night after brief reapplication of BiPAP nocturnally on night 2.
Overnight RN notes no episodes of desaturation below 90% on 3L.
OBJECTIVE:
Gen: comfortable, speaking in full sentences
Lungs: scattered expiratory wheeze, improved air movement bilaterally, no accessory muscle use this AM
CV: RRR, no murmur
Ext: no edema
LABS:
Repeat ABG 06:00 on 3L: pH 7.36, PaCO2 52, PaO2 71
ASSESSMENT/PLAN:
COPD exacerbation - improving. Hypercapnia resolving.
1. Wean to 2L NC as tolerated, target SpO2 88-92%
2. Continue nebs q4h
3. IV steroid: methylprednisolone 40 mg IV every 8 hours - plan transition to PO prednisone today
4. Hyperglycemia: glucose rose to 342 requiring insulin sliding scale - start SSI moderate scale q6h
5. Continue azithromycin, day 2
6. Ambulate with PT, check ambulatory sat
7. Anticipate discharge later today if ambulatory sats hold

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 PM
lines: PROGRESS NOTE - HD2 15:10
INTERVAL:
Pt ambulated 200 ft in hallway with RN at 13:40, SpO2 91% on 2L NC, RR 18, no dyspnea reported.
Off O2 trial at rest 14:10: SpO2 90% on room air over 20 min.
No accessory muscle use, no wheeze audible without stethoscope.
Tolerated regular diet. Denies nausea.
OBJECTIVE:
Lungs: mild expiratory wheeze at bases only, good air movement
CV: RRR
Neuro: alert, no tremor
CBG 12:00: 244, 4 units regular insulin given per sliding scale
ASSESSMENT/PLAN:
1. COPD exacerbation - resolved acute phase, back to home O2 requirement (2L nocturnal)
2. Transitioned off IV steroid to prednisone 40 mg PO daily to complete 5-day total course
3. Continue albuterol/ipratropium nebs, transition to home inhalers prior to discharge
4. Azithromycin - complete 5 day course PO
5. Hyperglycemia steroid-induced - counseled on home glucose checks BID while on prednisone
6. Inhaler technique reviewed with RN and pt, spacer provided
7. Discharge home today with daughter, pulm f/u in 1 week
8. Return precautions reviewed

documents.title: Discharge Summary - COPD Exacerbation
lines: DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admit HD1, discharged HD2
DISCHARGE DIAGNOSIS: Acute exacerbation of COPD with acute on chronic hypercapnic respiratory failure
SECONDARY: HTN, GERD, type 2 DM, osteoporosis, steroid-induced hyperglycemia
HOSPITAL COURSE:
74 yo F with GOLD III COPD presented with 3 days of worsening dyspnea and purulent sputum.
SpO2 84% at triage; required 4L NC to reach SpO2 89%.
Visible accessory muscle use with tripod positioning; respiratory rate 32; speaking 2 to 3 words at a time.
Two albuterol nebulizers in the ED with improved air movement; patient ambulating in hallway before admission decision.
ABG at 03:15: pH 7.29, PaCO2 64, PaO2 58 on 4L.
Placed on BiPAP 14/6 at 03:30 for work of breathing; remained on BiPAP continuously for 9 hours, then nocturnally on night 2.
Treated with IV steroid: methylprednisolone 40 mg IV every 8 hours, scheduled albuterol/ipratropium nebs, and azithromycin.
Repeat ABG HD2 06:00 on 3L: pH 7.36, PaCO2 52, PaO2 71.
Course complicated by hyperglycemia - glucose rose to 342 requiring insulin sliding scale, resolved with steroid taper to PO.
Weaned to 2L NC HD2 AM. Ambulated 200 ft with SpO2 91% on 2L. Room air rest sat 90%.
CXR showed hyperinflation without infiltrate. WBC peaked 13.2, down to 10.4.
DISCHARGE EXAM: T 36.9, HR 84, BP 128/74, RR 18, SpO2 91% on 2L, lungs with minimal basilar wheeze
DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
Prednisone 40 mg PO daily x 3 more days then stop
Azithromycin 250 mg PO daily x 3 more days
Tiotropium 18 mcg inh daily
Budesonide/formoterol 160/4.5 two puffs BID
Albuterol MDI 2 puffs q4h prn with spacer
Lisinopril 10 mg PO daily
Pantoprazole 40 mg PO daily
Alendronate 70 mg PO weekly
HOME O2: 2L NC nocturnal, unchanged from baseline
INSTRUCTIONS:
Check fingerstick glucose BID while on prednisone, call if > 300
Use spacer with MDI; technique reviewed and teach-back completed
Return for increased work of breathing, confusion, fever, or inability to speak full sentences
FOLLOW-UP: pulmonary clinic in 1 week; primary care in 2 weeks
Discharged home in stable condition with daughter at 16:40.
